regions.note: Large heading text in the page body. Resolvable by the full-image pass even after the detector's downsample to the input budget.

The gradient's floor: 8px text that the native-resolution tile pass resolves at exactly the recognizer's resolvable minimum. Any reduction in tile resolution drops this region, which is why it is here -- a tile-budget cut that costs small-text recall cannot pass unnoticed.
Gradient midpoint. Survives a modest tile-resolution reduction, so the fixture still reports *which* sizes a cut costs, not just that something broke.
Largest gradient run. Big enough that the full-image pass finds it too, so the gradient's upper end is not tile-dependent -- it exists to keep the failure attributable to resolution alone.

Text baked into a small embedded thumbnail. THIS is the case the tiled OCR pass exists for: the full-image pass downsamples it below resolvable size, so only the native-resolution tile pass can find it.
